group_bootstrap.assumption: Whole groups are sampled with replacement and treated as independent, comparable groups. Serial correlation and changing variability can invalidate population inference; these are exploratory sensitivity results, not new website measurements.

failure_model.assumption: Independent Bernoulli test outcomes at the pooled fitted failure rate, with a fixed representative batch size. This validates the model's tail probability, not software quality.

provenance.request_timing: Fresh HTTPS request, start through complete body read; includes network/TLS/server transfer, not browser rendering.

Simulation · resampling the recorded groups

For one simulation, Python randomly picks 20 recorded groups, allowing the same group to be picked more than once. Each picked group keeps its original five timings. Python calculates the average of the resulting 100 timings. It repeats this process 10,000 times.

This asks: how much would the study average move if we obtained another selection of groups like the recorded ones? It reuses real observations; it does not send new requests to ForeverMart.

Simulation resultValue
Recorded mean372.16 ms
Average of simulated study means372.18 ms
Absolute difference0.0235 ms
Exploratory 95% bootstrap interval365.56–380.99 ms
Spread of simulated means (bootstrap SE)4.01 ms
99% interval for Monte Carlo mean error372.08–372.28 ms
Fixed random seed20260901

The 95% interval describes sensitivity to group selection under the independent-group assumption. The separate 99% Monte Carlo interval describes numerical simulation noise. Serial measurements and unstable variability limit population conclusions. Neither interval establishes a website performance guarantee.

Simulation · checking the failure-count formula

The observed failure rate is 0%. A binomial model fitted directly to that rate produces zero failures in every simulated five-check round. This boundary result is expected; it cannot discover failures absent from the sample.

Model verificationValue

Do not interpret this as “the website can never fail.” More real coverage and later measurements are needed. Bootstrap timing simulation above remains useful because the recorded response times vary.

Calculation formulas

Group mean = sum of its five timings / 5; group range = maximum − minimum.

X̄ limits = grand mean ± 3 × average range / (2.326 × √5).
R limits = 0 and 2.114 × average range.

p̄ = total failed / total checks; p limits = p̄ ± 3√[p̄(1−p̄)/5], clipped to 0–1.

Percentiles use NumPy’s linear interpolation; standard deviation uses the sample denominator (n−1). The n=5 chart factors match the attached study and Levin/Rubin’s book, including D4 = 2.114. All display rounding happens after calculation.

ForeverMart · attached PDF study · 7 October 2026. No textbook-answer comparison is made for website measurements. Identical data, settings and seed reproduce the simulation; changing the seed changes random draws, not the recorded calculations.

Tools: Python, NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. References: original attached report.pdf and retained study evidence; Levin/Rubin, Statistics for Management, Chapter 10 / Appendix Table 9; NIST mean/range chart guidance; SciPy bootstrap method documentation.
